Brand Story.description: Pizza My Heart was founded right on Capitola Beach, and is still there. It’s not much larger than the average bedroom, but that tiny Capitola restaurant has become a landmark for surfers and beachgoers alike. Stoked with the success in Capitola, Pizza My Heart opened in downtown Santa Cruz a few years later. This was a big upgrade for both local and tourists as there was actually room to sit down and enjoy a slice. After the ’89 earthquake damaged our building, we moved to our current location on Pacific Avenue, bringing along our great pizza and even greater customers. In 1997 the founders decided they could use more time surfing and decided to merge with Pizza A Go Go, another concept dedicated to great food, customer service and fun. We’ve grown a lot since then, but the thing that made us great in Capitola in 1981 is still what makes us great today. Fresh, hand tossed pizza, the best local ingredients we can find, and customers who reward us with their business and smiles every day. We are family owned and have no plans to franchise or sell out. We are committed to serving the best pizza in California and we believe that staying family owned is the only way to do that. We open a few new restaurants each year to serve a few more customers. If you’ve been with us from the beginning, or joined any time along the way – Thank You! If you haven’t yet discovered Pizza My Heart, we invite you to come on in. We promise it’s a habit you’ll come to love.

Founder's Story.description: Stoked to be part of the celebrations for the 60th Anniversary the epic surf film The Endless Summer. Scan the code and get a free pass to Endless Summer events including the screening on the Santa Cruz Boardwalk on Friday July 12. Chuck Hammers, the owner of Pizza My Heart, has shared several insights about pizza and life that reflect his unique journey and philosophy. Hammers, who transitioned from a career in geophysics to building a successful pizza chain, emphasizes the importance of community and resilience. He often describes himself humorously as 'just a pizza guy' but has found himself in significant situations, such as attending the State of the Union address. This opportunity came after his Capitola Village restaurant sustained extensive storm damage, highlighting the importance of federal and community support in recovery efforts. Hammers believes in the power of optimism and collaboration. He notes that despite being competitors, local businesses often work together to overcome challenges, especially after natural disasters. This cooperative spirit is essential for the survival and success of small businesses. Furthermore, Hammers has effectively utilized creative marketing strategies, such as the hugely popular Pizza My Heart T-shirts. These shirts, which come with a free slice of pizza, symbolize local pride and have become a cultural icon in the area, demonstrating his innovative approach to business. Overall, Hammers' comments on pizza and life reflect a blend of humor, optimism, and a strong sense of community, emphasizing resilience and the importance of working together to achieve success.
